experiments.title: RAG Threshold Sweep Reproduction + Random-Retrieval Baseline
addresses_questions: Does recovering the full RAG threshold sweep confirm 0.84 as the true F1-argmax, and does retrieval performance (MRR 0.856, hit@1 0.793) exceed a random/no-retrieval baseline by a quantifiable margin on the 8-document/44-chunk corpus?
experiments.hypothesis: H4: the deployed RAG_MIN_SIMILARITY=0.85 threshold is a deliberate precision-favoring choice just below the F1-argmax (expected 0.84), and e5-small/heading-chunking retrieval clears a random-baseline retriever by a non-trivial margin on this corpus, i.e. the reported MRR/hit@1 reflect real semantic retrieval skill, not corpus-size artefact (bench.py's own `degenerate` flag already warns k=5 over ~44 chunks is 35%+ coverage).
experiments.procedure: (1) Run `python -m rag.calibrate` from llm-service/ (verified CLI at llm-service/rag/calibrate.py, argparse: --model e5-small [default], --strategy heading [default]) against the live sure_rag Postgres collection (confirmed present via `psql -l`); capture the full precision/recall/F1 sweep table it prints and read off the argmax row, comparing to the deployed threshold. (2) Run `python -m rag.bench` (llm-service/rag/bench.py) with default args and record each BenchResult's `degenerate` property (`coverage_at_k >= 0.35`) alongside MRR/hit@1/hit@3/hit@5 for every (model, strategy) pair -- this field already exists in the dataclass, no new code needed. (3) Author a new small script `llm-service/rag/random_baseline.py` that reuses bench.py's `run_combination` machinery but replaces `store.search(...)` with a call that returns `k` chunk ids drawn uniformly at random (fixed seed, report the seed) from the full chunk_all(strategy) list for the same EVAL_QUERIES, computing hit@1/hit@3/hit@5/MRR the identical way (via rag.evalset.hit_at_k / reciprocal_rank) so the comparison is apples-to-apples. Run it against the same 8-document/44-chunk corpus and the same k. (4) Compute the margin: e5-small's MRR/hit@1 minus the random baseline's MRR/hit@1. (5) Write a short paragraph (not code) citing literature_review_sources.json id 16 (per-corpus threshold calibration) and id 17 (Semantic Illusion/HALT-RAG, hallucination-mitigation limits) to scope the 0.85 threshold claim.
experiments.required_environment: anaconda python3 (has psycopg/pgvector/sentence-transformers already installed) run from llm-service/ with a working RAG_DATABASE_URL pointing at the live local `sure_rag` Postgres DB (default `postgresql:///sure_rag`, confirmed reachable). No GPU needed -- e5-small is a 384-dim CPU-fast embedding model. Must confirm `store.count(collection)` is non-zero before running (calibrate.py/bench.py print an explicit error and exit 1 if the collection is empty, in which case `python -m rag.ingest` must be run first).
experiments.baselines: vision.md/research_task.md's already-published figures: e5-small/heading MRR=0.856, hit@1=0.793, F1-argmax at threshold 0.84 vs. deployed 0.85 (F1 0.951 vs 0.906 per research_goals.json's strong criterion). This experiment either reproduces or corrects those exact numbers, and adds a random-baseline number that does not yet exist anywhere in the repo or docs.
experiments.metrics: precision(t), recall(t), F1(t) for t swept in calibrate.py's own 0.01-step loop; hit@1, hit@3, hit@5, MRR (reciprocal_rank averaged over EVAL_QUERIES) for e5-small/heading vs. the new random baseline; BenchResult.degenerate boolean per combination; margin = MRR_e5small - MRR_random and hit@1_e5small - hit@1_random.
experiments.ablations: None required for minimum viable; the random-baseline retriever itself functions as the one ablation arm against the production retriever (vary retrieval strategy: learned embedding vs. uniform-random selection, holding queries/corpus/k fixed).
experiments.success_criteria: Strong (matches research_goals.json G1 strong): calibrate.py's sweep reproduces F1-argmax at/near 0.84 (or reports the corrected true argmax if different); bench.py's degenerate flag is reported; random_baseline.py shows e5-small's MRR/hit@1 exceeding random by a stated, non-negligible margin; paragraph cites sources 16/17. Minimum viable (matches G1 minimum_viable): if random_baseline.py cannot be finished, report calibrate.py's sweep table and bench.py's degenerate flag as disclosed caveats without a quantified baseline, still citing sources 16/17.
experiments.end_stage_rationale: The strong success criterion is itself built on two sweeps/comparisons: calibrate.py's full threshold sweep (an implicit sensitivity sweep across many thresholds) plus a genuinely new baseline-retriever ablation (learned vs. random retrieval) that must be authored, not merely read. This is the same class of 'sweep + comparison-arm' work the task instructions flag as end_stage=4 for G8, so G1 is held to the same bar.
open_decisions: Whether `postgresql:///sure_rag` (the default RAG_DATABASE_URL) resolves correctly for the anaconda python's psycopg without an explicit user/password -- confirmed only that `psql -l` can see the DB via peer auth; the Python client's auth path was not separately tested and should be checked with a one-line `python -c "from rag.store import VectorStore; VectorStore(dim=384).count('e5-small:heading')"` smoke test before committing to the full run.

Exact random seed and sampling scheme for random_baseline.py (uniform over all chunks vs. uniform over docs-then-chunk) is not specified anywhere upstream and must be chosen and documented by whoever implements it -- uniform-over-chunks is recommended since that's what real retrieval competes against, but this is a genuine design choice, not something read off existing code.

experiments.title: Eval-Harness / Production Rule-Path Consistency Trace
addresses_questions: Do llm-service/eval.py's rule-computation path and backend/main.py's apply_rule_override path remain consistent (no residual eval/production drift) after the drift-bug fix that motivates the paper's opening narrative?
experiments.hypothesis: H1 (precondition): both llm-service/eval.py and backend/main.py resolve their rule-based severity computation to the exact same backend/rules.py functions (evaluate/evaluate_status), with no re-implemented or copy-drifted logic remaining anywhere in either path, i.e. the historical drift bug narrated in eval.py's own docstring has been fully and correctly fixed, not just partially patched.
experiments.procedure: This is a pure static-analysis / code-trace goal requiring no execution beyond one verification script. (1) Confirm by direct inspection (already done for this design pass, re-verify at execution time in case the code has changed) that llm-service/eval.py inserts backend/ onto sys.path and does `import rules` (not a local copy), and that its `rule_status()` helper calls `rules.evaluate_status(sc['sensor'], sc['vision'])` -- the exact function backend/rules.py exports. (2) Confirm backend/main.py line 31 does `import rules` (same module object, since both processes point sys.path at the same backend/rules.py file on disk) and that `rule_based_decision()` (line 303) calls `rules.evaluate(...)` while `apply_rule_override()` (line 329) calls `rule_based_decision()` internally then compares `SEVERITY.get(rule['status'],0) > SEVERITY.get(parsed.get('status'),0)`, where `SEVERITY = rules.SEVERITY` (line 62) -- i.e. the exact same severity table. (3) Write a small `analysis/g2_consistency_check.py` script that imports `rules` once, then imports eval.py's `rule_status` and backend's `rule_based_decision` (via VisionFrame/SensorReading pydantic wrappers built from eval.py's 8 SCENARIOS dicts) and asserts, for all 8 scenarios, that `rule_status(sc) == rule_based_decision(vision_obj, sensor_obj)['status']` -- since both ultimately call the identical rules.py functions this should trivially pass, but running it converts 'the code looks the same' into 'a script asserted equality and printed PASS for 8/8'. (4) Write the one-paragraph Methodology/Discussion audit note.
experiments.required_environment: Any Python with pydantic installed (backend/requirements.txt: pydantic>=2.9.0) to construct VisionFrame/SensorReading instances -- the anaconda env or backend's own dependency set both work; no LLM, no GPU, runs in well under a second.
experiments.baselines: The paper's own opening narrative (eval.py's docstring): a previously-fixed drift bug where a copied rule engine said 'warning' for the fish_count==0 case while production said 'ok'. This experiment's baseline is that specific historical failure mode -- success means confirming it cannot recur because both paths import the same module object, not merely that outputs happen to match today.
experiments.metrics: Binary per-scenario agreement (8/8 expected); a structural check (import-path trace) reported as pass/fail, not a numeric metric.
experiments.ablations: None applicable -- this is a mechanism/consistency audit, not a measurement with tunable parameters.
experiments.success_criteria: Strong (matches G2 strong): the trace confirms no re-implemented severity logic exists anywhere in either path, and the 8/8 consistency-check script passes. Minimum viable (matches G2 minimum_viable): if any divergence sub-path is found (e.g. a stale local copy somewhere not caught by this design pass's inspection), report file/line and disclose it as a newly-found, analogous drift bug rather than hiding it -- this is itself a valid, reportable finding per the goal's own failure-mode framing.
experiments.end_stage_rationale: No sweep or ablation is applicable to a single consistency trace; this is a primary experiment (not pilot validation, hence not end_stage=1) whose minimum_viable criterion is already the strong criterion's fallback, so end_stage=3 (full run for the minimum_viable criterion) is the correct ceiling.

experiments.title: Behavioral Four-Bucket Classification of AQUA-1B Through apply_rule_override
addresses_questions: When AQUA-1B's raw eval.py output is actually passed through apply_rule_override, what is the observed four-bucket distribution (agrees / under-calls-and-escalated / over-calls / unparseable-defaulted-to-ok), and does manual coding of the model's reasoning text reveal at least one non-enumerable failure mode the rule engine cannot catch, grounding H2's scope boundary?
experiments.hypothesis: H1/H2: AQUA-1B + LoRA adapter's raw output, when run through the same apply_rule_override() safety net used in production, falls into a small number of behaviorally distinct buckets (agree / under-call-escalated / over-call / unparseable-defaults-to-ok) rather than uniformly agreeing with the rule engine; and at least one of the model's free-text reasoning strings will contain a factual or qualitative judgment (e.g. about *why* a parameter is concerning) that the enumerable threshold-based rule engine structurally cannot express, illustrating H2's enumerable/non-enumerable scope boundary.
experiments.procedure: (1) Write a new script `analysis/g3_dual_layer_behavior.py` (not a monkeypatch of eval.py, since eval.py's model_status() only returns a bare status string for pass/fail comparison and never calls apply_rule_override -- this is a genuine gap between what exists and what the goal needs). For each of eval.py's 8 SCENARIOS: call `inference.generate_decision(snapshot)` directly (the same function eval.py's model_status() wraps) to get AQUA-1B's raw parsed dict (status/reasoning/recommendations/sources); construct a backend.main.VisionFrame and SensorReading from the scenario's vision/sensor dicts (adding the required `timestamp`/`frame_id`/`tracks` fields VisionFrame needs, per backend/test_decision.py's own `_vision()`/`_sensor()` helper pattern); call `backend.main.apply_rule_override(parsed, vision_obj, sensor_obj)`; classify the (pre-override status, post-override status, rule_override flag) triple into the four buckets: agree (rule_override absent, model status == rule status), under-calls-and-escalated (rule_override True), over-calls (model status has higher SEVERITY than rule status -- apply_rule_override never downgrades, so this bucket is only detectable by separately computing rule_based_decision() and comparing severities, not from rule_override alone), unparseable-defaulted-to-ok (generate_decision's except branch fired, i.e. raw output had no matching `{...}` JSON, recognizable via reasoning field equal to raw[:500] and status=='ok' with no sources-derived confidence). (2) Before running, export `AQUA_ADAPTER_PATH=./llm-service/sure-aqua-adapter` (see environment_facts_verified: without this the adapter silently does not load) and record `Path('llm-service/sure-aqua-adapter/adapters.safetensors').stat().st_mtime` plus `git log -1 --format=%H -- llm-service/sure-aqua-adapter` as adapter-provenance evidence (note: the adapter directory itself may not be git-tracked -- check `git status llm-service/sure-aqua-adapter` first and fall back to mtime + a note if it is gitignored). (3) Separately run `python -m pytest backend/test_decision.py -v` (anaconda python; already has pydantic via fastapi stack) and record pass/fail as mechanism-correctness evidence, explicitly not substituted for the behavioral result. (4) Manually read and code all 8 `reasoning` strings for factual/citation accuracy (a human/manual step -- the researcher reads 8 short Turkish strings and annotates each with accurate/inaccurate/non-enumerable-observation). (5) Cross-reference EXP01's F1=0.906 residual-hallucination figure (production threshold 0.85) as grounding for H2. (6) Draft the Precision Check paragraph citing sources 11, 26 (SIS/IEC 61511), 12 (RL-shielding).
experiments.required_environment: anaconda python3 (has torch 2.10.0, mlx-lm 0.30.7 for the mlx backend) run from llm-service/ with `AQUA_ADAPTER_PATH` exported. Requires local LLM inference: AQUA-1B (~1.9GB, confirmed cached at ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--KurmaAI--AQUA-1B) + the LoRA adapter (confirmed present at llm-service/sure-aqua-adapter/adapters.safetensors, 8.0MB) via mlx-lm on the M4 Pro's mlx backend (BACKEND='mlx' since torch.backends.mps.is_available()==True). This is genuinely runnable on this machine -- not a stub -- but is the first experiment in this design set that actually invokes the LLM, so budget real (if short) wall-clock time: 8 short-prompt generations at max_tokens=512, temp=0.3 on a 1B model via mlx should be well under a minute total based on the loop's own token budget, though first-call model load adds ~5-15s.
experiments.baselines: backend/test_decision.py's existing pass/fail (mechanism-correctness baseline, already exists and is expected to pass); EXP01's F1=0.906 (production threshold 0.85) as the residual-hallucination-risk baseline that H2's scope claim leans on; eval.py's own rule_status() output per scenario as the rule-engine ground truth each bucket is measured against.
experiments.metrics: 4-bucket distribution over n=8 scenarios (counts and percentages); pytest pass/fail count for test_decision.py (currently 17 test functions, one skipped without torch); manual-coding tally of accurate vs. inaccurate vs. illustrates-non-enumerable-boundary reasoning strings (n=8, qualitative).
experiments.ablations: None required by G3's success criteria; adapter-provenance is recorded as a note, not swept (H1-3, retraining a v2 adapter, is explicitly excluded from this goal per research_goals.json's merge_rationale).
experiments.success_criteria: Strong (matches G3 strong): 8-scenario 4-bucket table produced with adapter provenance recorded; test_decision.py passes and is reported separately; >=1 non-enumerable failure mode identified in the manual coding; Precision Check paragraph drafted citing 11/26/12. Minimum viable (matches G3 minimum_viable): if AQUA-1B output is mostly unparseable, report 'malformed-output fail-safe is the dominant observed pathway, not severity-correction' as the H1 finding -- itself a valid, differently-framed safety claim; if none of the 8 reasoning strings show an inaccuracy, report the n=8 illustration as weaker but still valid for H2.
experiments.end_stage_rationale: No parameter sweep or multi-arm ablation is called for by G3's own success criteria (H1-3's optional LoRA retrain is explicitly excluded from this goal's scope) -- the work is a single behavioral run plus manual qualitative coding, so end_stage=3 (full run for minimum_viable, which strong extends with the manual-coding depth) applies, not end_stage=4.
open_decisions: The over-calls bucket is not directly observable from apply_rule_override's `rule_override` flag alone (that flag only fires on escalation) -- the analysis script must separately call `rule_based_decision()` and compare SEVERITY values to detect the case where the model's status is MORE severe than the rule engine's, which apply_rule_override correctly leaves untouched (by design, it never downgrades). This bucket-detection logic needs to be written carefully; it is not a one-line check.

llm-service/test-adapter/adapters.safetensors (4.0MB) exists alongside sure-aqua-adapter/adapters.safetensors (8.0MB) with no README/docstring explanation found for what test-adapter is or when it was produced -- before this experiment runs, confirm sure-aqua-adapter (not test-adapter) is the one deployed via docker-compose.yml's AQUA_ADAPTER_PATH=/adapter mount, and note in the provenance write-up that test-adapter's origin is unknown and excluded.

Whether llm-service/sure-aqua-adapter/ is git-tracked (for a commit-hash-based provenance claim) or gitignored (forcing mtime-only provenance) was not checked in this design pass and must be checked with `git check-ignore -v llm-service/sure-aqua-adapter/adapters.safetensors` before writing the provenance note.

experiments.title: Agentic Tool-Routing Reproduction, Constant-Answer Audit, and Scenario Expansion
addresses_questions: Do bench_agent.py's existing AQUA-1B (0%/0%) and AQUA-7B (60%/50%-constant-answer) figures reproduce on re-run, does the constant-answer detection logic hold up against the actual run log, and does genuinely growing the scenario count past n=5 preserve or soften the 'small LLMs fail at tool-calling' negative result?
experiments.hypothesis: H3: small local LLMs (AQUA-1B base, and AQUA-7B/Mistral-4bit at the deployed prompt/format) cannot reliably drive the closed-menu agentic tool-selection loop -- AQUA-1B fails the output-format requirement outright (~0% format compliance) and AQUA-7B, while more format-compliant, is not actually discriminating between scenarios but emitting a constant tool choice that happens to be correct in some of them (len(set(chosen tools))==1 across scenarios) -- and this negative result holds, or is only mildly softened, when the scenario set genuinely grows past the current n=5.
experiments.procedure: (1) Re-run `python -m agent.bench_agent --model KurmaAI/AQUA-1B` and `python -m agent.bench_agent --model KurmaAI/AQUA-7B` fresh (both weights confirmed cached locally) from llm-service/, recording format compliance %, selection %, and the constant-answer flag exactly as the script computes them (verified at llm-service/agent/bench_agent.py: `constant = len(chosen) >= 3 and len(set(chosen)) == 1`), to check reproduction of the README's reported AQUA-1B 0%/0% and AQUA-7B 60%/50%-constant-answer figures. (2) Audit the constant-answer logic against the actual run's printed per-scenario `tool=` lines (not just the final aggregate) to manually confirm `get_sensor_trend` (or whichever tool) was genuinely chosen in all 5 scenarios for AQUA-7B, i.e. that the 50% figure really is a constant-answer artifact and not a coincidence of the aggregate math. (3) Author >=4 new `Scenario` entries in bench_agent.py's SCENARIOS tuple using the existing `Scenario`/`StaticDataSource`/`_sensors()`/`_falling()`/`_vision()` helper machinery (confirmed present, e.g. a scenario with rising temperature + normal DO to test discrimination against the existing 'oxygen falling' case, a scenario with pH improving rather than degrading, a scenario combining low activity + falling TDS, a scenario with borderline-but-safe values to test restraint like the existing 'everything normal' scenario) -- spanning the same failure categories (format, selection, constant-answer, restraint) as the original 5. (4) Re-run the full (now >=9-scenario) benchmark against both models and report the resulting format/selection/constant-answer figures. (5) Explicitly do NOT use `--repeat N` as a substitute for new scenarios -- confirmed in code that `make_generator`'s `generate()` calls `inference._generate(prompt, temp=0.0, ...)`, i.e. greedy decoding, so `--repeat` produces byte-identical outputs and adds zero information; this must be stated explicitly per G4's own minimum_viable clause. (6) Cite source 21 to scope the constant-answer-detection technique as a known-artifact-detection principle applied to a new task, not a novel invention.
experiments.required_environment: anaconda python3 (torch + mlx-lm) run from llm-service/. Requires local LLM inference for BOTH AQUA-1B (~1.9GB) and AQUA-7B (~14GB, 3-shard safetensors) -- both confirmed cached locally, both loadable via mlx-lm on this M4 Pro's mlx backend. This is the highest-latency experiment in the set involving real inference: 7B generation at README's own historical rate of ~11.9s per scenario x (5 original + >=4 new) x however many agent-loop steps each scenario takes (loop.py's PLAN_MAX_TOKENS budget, not re-verified line-by-line in this pass) could plausibly run 10-30 minutes for the AQUA-7B leg alone; AQUA-1B is much faster. Flag as the one experiment in this design set worth timing explicitly on a short dry run (e.g. 1 scenario) before committing to the full >=9-scenario x 2-model matrix.
experiments.baselines: README.md's existing published table: AQUA-1B 0%/0%; AQUA-7B (Mistral, 4-bit) 60% format / 50% selection / 3.6 mean steps / 11.9s mean duration, with the existing 'constant answer' framing already present in the current bench_agent.py source code (not something this experiment invents).
experiments.metrics: format compliance % (`res.format_ok`), tool-selection accuracy % among scenarios with `acceptable` sets (`res.selection_ok`), mean steps, mean duration in seconds, constant-answer boolean flag, all computed identically to bench_agent.py's own `main()` aggregation logic, both on the original n=5 set and the expanded n>=9 set for direct before/after comparison.
experiments.ablations: The natural ablation here is scenario-count (n=5 vs. n>=9) at fixed model and fixed decoding (temp=0.0); this directly operationalizes the brainstorm's Ablation row 3 ('agent benchmark too small to generalize').
experiments.success_criteria: Strong (matches G4 strong): fresh re-run confirms the existing AQUA-1B/AQUA-7B figures; constant-answer audit confirms the flag is genuine against the real log; >=4 new scenarios authored and full benchmark re-run on both models; source 21 cited to scope the novelty claim. Minimum viable (matches G4 minimum_viable): if new scenarios are not authored in time, report the existing n=5/2-model result plainly as a disclosed limitation, still perform the reproducibility re-run and log audit (these require no new scenario-authoring work), and explicitly state that `--repeat N` does not constitute a sample-size increase.
experiments.end_stage_rationale: Scenario-count expansion is a genuine robustness check, not a formal ablation grid/sweep over a continuous parameter the way G1/G6/G7/G8 are -- it is closer to 'grow the test set and re-run,' which the minimum_viable clause explicitly treats as separable from the reproducibility re-run. end_stage=3 (full run for minimum_viable, strong criterion layered on top) is appropriate; end_stage=4 is reserved for goals whose strong criterion is inherently a parametric sweep.
open_decisions: Whether AQUA_ADAPTER_PATH should be set for this experiment is genuinely ambiguous: bench_agent.py's purpose (per its own docstring) is testing the BASE model's tool-calling capability, which arguably should be measured un-adapted (adapter untouched, ADAPTER_PATH empty, matching the historical README run if that run also had it unset) -- but this was not independently confirmed for the ORIGINAL README figures being reproduced here. Before running, check whether any AQUA_ADAPTER_PATH env var was set when the original 0%/0%-and-60%/50% numbers were produced (grep shell history / any run logs / ask the research team) so the reproduction run matches the original condition exactly.

Exact wording/content of the >=4 new Scenario entries is not prescribable from existing code alone (the existing 5 were hand-authored to span specific failure categories) -- this requires domain judgment about what other realistic sensor/vision patterns are worth testing and is left to whoever executes this experiment, using the existing 5 as a style template.

llm-service/agent/loop.py's PLAN_MAX_TOKENS value and its effect on AQUA-7B step count/duration was not read in this design pass -- worth a quick check before the full run to avoid an unexpectedly long tail (the docstring already warns a mis-set 512-token narration budget once stretched a 7B run from minutes to half an hour).

experiments.title: Vision Dataset Train/Val Leakage Audit (510-image sure_dataset)
addresses_questions: Does a clip/video-level leakage audit of the full 510-image vision dataset confirm no train/val leakage beyond the already-caught ogretmen case, protecting the headline mAP50/precision/recall figures?
experiments.hypothesis: XC-1 (protective control): the 412-image train / 98-image val split of data/sure_dataset (confirmed: exactly 412 files in train/images, 98 in val/images) contains no frame from the same source video/clip in both splits, distinct from the already-documented and already-corrected ogretmen leakage case (MODEL_RAPORU.md: ogretmen used the SAME folder for train and val by construction, and its metrics are already flagged invalid and excluded from headline numbers) -- i.e. sure_v1's mAP50/precision/recall figures are not inflated by near-duplicate frames crossing the split.
experiments.procedure: (1) List all filenames in data/sure_dataset/train/images and data/sure_dataset/val/images (confirmed pattern: `frame_XXXX.jpg` and `videoN_frame_XXXX.jpg`/`.txt` pairs also appear separately under data/frames/ -- clarify at execution time whether sure_dataset/{train,val}/images is a curated subset or the same pool, since data/frames/ contains videoN_frame_* filenames that encode source-video identity directly in the name). (2) Group filenames by inferred source (video number prefix where present, e.g. `video6_frame_0099`; for plain `frame_NNNN.jpg` names with no video prefix, source is ambiguous from filename alone and must be checked another way -- e.g. file timestamp/EXIF adjacency, or checking whether a separate manifest/label file records source video). (3) For every source group that has any frames in train, check whether that same source group also has any frames in val; report any such group as a leak. (4) As a secondary/optional check per XC-1's own 'optional perceptual-hash near-duplicate check', compute a perceptual hash (e.g. via a small script using PIL + a simple average-hash, since no dedicated perceptual-hash library was confirmed installed) for every image and flag any train/val pair with hash distance below a stated threshold as a near-duplicate candidate, manually reviewing any hits. (5) Cross-check the result explicitly against the already-known and already-corrected ogretmen leakage (data/ogretmen.yaml pointing train and val at the identical images/ folder) to confirm this audit is checking sure_v1's split, not re-discovering the already-known and already-excluded ogretmen issue.
experiments.required_environment: Any Python with PIL/numpy (already available in the anaconda env) -- pure filesystem/image-hash analysis, no GPU, no model inference, seconds to low minutes for 510 images.
experiments.baselines: MODEL_RAPORU.md's already-documented ogretmen leakage (train==val folder, mAP50=0.918, explicitly flagged invalid and excluded) as the known-positive-control leak this audit method must be capable of catching; sure_v1's current headline figures (mAP50 0.840, precision 0.858, recall 0.719, epoch 77 per the 2026-08-26 correction) as the numbers this audit protects if clean.
experiments.metrics: count of cross-split source-group collisions (target: 0, beyond the already-excluded ogretmen case which is not part of sure_dataset at all); count of near-duplicate image pairs below the chosen perceptual-hash distance threshold (reported even if 0).
experiments.ablations: None -- this is a single audit, not a parametrized measurement, though the perceptual-hash distance threshold choice functions as a sensitivity check worth trying at 2-3 values if any borderline near-duplicates are found.
experiments.success_criteria: Strong (matches G5 strong): filename/timestamp-adjacency check (plus optional perceptual-hash check) across all 510 images confirms zero cross-split leakage beyond the already-caught-and-corrected ogretmen case; reported as an Experimental Setup data-integrity paragraph closing Ablation row 7. Minimum viable (matches G5 minimum_viable): if further leakage IS found, report exactly which images/videos are affected and state a corrected, caveated headline vision number rather than shipping the uncorrected 0.840/0.858/0.719 figures.
experiments.end_stage_rationale: A single audit with an optional secondary check, not a parameter sweep in the G1/G6/G7/G8 sense (the perceptual-hash threshold is a minor sensitivity note, not the goal's central claim) -- end_stage=3 for the full minimum_viable-or-strong run.
open_decisions: Whether data/sure_dataset/{train,val}/images filenames reliably encode source-video identity was not fully confirmed in this design pass -- a quick `ls data/sure_dataset/train/images | head -50` and `ls data/sure_dataset/val/images` full listing (not just the first 5 shown during this design pass) is needed to determine whether the video-prefix naming convention seen in data/frames/ (videoN_frame_NNNN) also holds inside sure_dataset, or whether sure_dataset uses a different (possibly re-numbered, source-anonymized) naming scheme that would require a different leakage-detection method (e.g. perceptual hashing as the PRIMARY method, not secondary).

No perceptual-hash library (e.g. imagehash) was confirmed installed in either environment during this design pass -- confirm availability or plan to implement a minimal average-hash inline with PIL + numpy only.

experiments.title: Export-Format Accuracy-Loss Mechanism: Multi-Session Latency Variance + ONNX-vs-TorchScript Per-Image Diff
addresses_questions: Is the CoreML/ANE 9.0ms p50 latency figure stable across multiple sessions, does a fresh val() run on best.pt reproduce the current headline vision numbers with no new epoch-73-style discrepancy, and does a per-image ONNX-vs-TorchScript detection diff support or refute the shared-post-processing-path causal explanation for their matching accuracy loss?
experiments.hypothesis: H6: (a) the CoreML/ANE p50=9.0ms/p95=9.5ms latency figure is a stable characteristic of the export, not a lucky single sample; (b) a fresh model.val() run on sure_models/sure_v1/weights/best.pt reproduces the current epoch-77 headline figures (P 0.858/R 0.719/mAP50 0.840, per MODEL_RAPORU.md's 2026-08-26 correction) with no new discrepancy of the kind that previously mis-selected epoch 73; (c) ONNX and TorchScript produce near-identical per-image detections on the 98-image val set (high IoU-overlap agreement), which would be direct mechanistic evidence for MODEL_RAPORU.md's claim that their matching -0.0104 mAP50 loss comes from a SHARED post-processing path rather than coincidental independent numerical noise.
experiments.procedure: (1) Re-run `python vision-service/export_bench.py` (confirmed CLI: `main()` at line 311, args `--formats` [default: all six configs already in MODEL_RAPORU.md's table], `--skip-export` to reuse existing exports, `--json FILE`) end-to-end against sure_models/sure_v1/weights/best.pt and data/sure_dataset.yaml, recording the full six-configuration table (pt/mps, pt/cpu, onnx/cpu, onnx-int8/cpu, coreml/ANE, torchscript/cpu: p50/p95/FPS/ΔmAP50/size) and the exact git commit hash (`git rev-parse HEAD`) + date at run time. (2) Repeat the CoreML/ANE row specifically >=3 separate times (separate process invocations, not just repeated in-process loops, to catch session-level thermal/scheduling variance) and report mean±std or min/max range for p50/p95, not a single sample. (3) Run `model.val()` (via a small script or export_bench.py's own val-only path) on best.pt fresh, recording the exact commit hash/date, and diff against MODEL_RAPORU.md's stated epoch-77 numbers to confirm no new epoch-73-style discrepancy exists. (4) Write a new script `analysis/g6_onnx_torchscript_diff.py` that loads both the ONNX and TorchScript exports (already produced by export_bench.py under sure_models/sure_v1/export/), runs both against the same 98 val images, and for each image computes IoU between each ONNX detection box and its best-matching TorchScript detection box (Hungarian or greedy matching), reporting the distribution of per-image IoU-overlap and the count of images where the two exports' detections differ meaningfully (e.g. IoU < 0.9 for a matched pair, or a differing detection count). (5) Cite source 8 (GitHub issue threads on export/NMS mechanisms) and source 9 (TensorRT/INT8 quantization literature) to contextualize the -0.0082 to -0.0104 ΔmAP50 range within the literature's normal 0.5-2.0pp calibrated band.
experiments.required_environment: anaconda python3 (ultralytics 8.4.14 confirmed importable) run from vision-service/, mps device available (Apple M4 Pro). CoreML export/inference requires coremltools (not independently confirmed installed in this design pass -- flag as an open_decision). No GPU/CUDA needed or usable; TensorRT/Jetson rows remain categorically unmeasurable on this machine per jetson_bench.py's own docstring.
experiments.baselines: MODEL_RAPORU.md's 2026-08-26 corrected export table (six rows, exact values quoted in this design's verified vision.md excerpt): CoreML/ANE p50=9.0ms/p95=9.5ms/mAP50=0.8298/ΔmAP50=-0.0097; ONNX cpu ΔmAP50=-0.0104; TorchScript cpu ΔmAP50=-0.0104 (identical to 4 decimal places on mAP50-95: 0.5867 both); pt/mps baseline mAP50=0.8395.
experiments.metrics: p50/p95 latency (ms) per format per session, mean±std across sessions for CoreML/ANE specifically; FPS; ΔmAP50 relative to pt/mps baseline; model size (MB); per-image IoU-overlap distribution (median, min, % of images below a stated agreement threshold) between ONNX and TorchScript detections.
experiments.ablations: The multi-session repetition (>=3 separate CoreML runs) is itself the variance-characterization ablation requested by Ablation row 1 ('edge latency advantage is a batch-size-1/single-device/thermal artifact'); the ONNX-vs-TorchScript diff is the mechanism-test ablation for the causal claim.
experiments.success_criteria: Strong (matches G6 strong): six-configuration table reproduced with commit hash; >=3-session CoreML variance reported as mean±std/range; fresh val() confirms no new discrepancy; per-image diff run and IoU-overlap agreement reported as direct evidence for/against the shared-post-processing-path claim; sources 8/9 cited. Minimum viable (matches G6 minimum_viable): if multi-session variance is high, widen the reported range and state the headline as a mean, not a single-run guarantee; if the per-image diff shows meaningful divergence despite matching aggregate mAP50, downgrade the causal claim to 'coincidental match, mechanism unconfirmed.'
experiments.end_stage_rationale: The strong success criterion is explicitly a multi-axis sweep/comparison: six export configurations, repeated >=3x for one of them to characterize variance, plus a dedicated per-image mechanistic diff between two of the configurations -- directly analogous to G8's example of end_stage=4 for sweep-based strong criteria.
open_decisions: coremltools' presence in the anaconda environment was not confirmed in this design pass (only ultralytics/torch/mlx were checked) -- must verify before assuming the CoreML export/re-measurement leg is runnable without new installs.

export_bench.py's exact val()-only invocation path (whether a `--skip-export` flag alone re-triggers a val() pass, or whether a small separate script is needed to call `YOLO(weights).val(data=...)` directly) was not traced line-by-line in this design pass beyond confirming the two `main()` functions and their argparse signatures exist -- read vision-service/export_bench.py's body (beyond the docstring/header read in this pass) before writing the re-run script.

The IoU-matching algorithm for the per-image ONNX-vs-TorchScript diff (greedy vs. Hungarian assignment, and the IoU threshold that counts as 'agreement' vs. 'divergence') is a genuine design choice not specified anywhere upstream and must be fixed and documented by whoever implements g6_onnx_torchscript_diff.py.

experiments.title: Vision Operating-Point Safety Trace: Fish-Per-Frame Distribution + Confidence-Threshold PR Sweep
addresses_questions: How rare is a full-frame miss (fish_count==0) under 0.719 per-instance recall given the actual val-set fish-per-frame distribution, and does a confidence-threshold sweep confirm precision=0.858/recall=0.719 as the true F1-argmax operating point?
experiments.hypothesis: H7: given the val-set's actual fish-per-frame distribution (98 images / 1525 fish per MODEL_RAPORU.md, i.e. ~15.6 fish/frame on average) and per-instance recall of 0.719, a full-frame miss (the rules.py-triggering fish_count==0 case) is numerically rare under current operating conditions IF frames are typically dense -- but this must be checked, not assumed, since a materially sparse subset of frames (1-2 fish) would make full-frame misses far more probable than the average recall figure suggests, changing the safety-relevance framing from reassuring to urgent; separately, the deployed confidence threshold that yields P=0.858/R=0.719 is confirmed (or shown not to be) the true F1-argmax across a 2-3-point confidence sweep.
experiments.procedure: (1) Load the ground-truth labels for all 98 val images (data/sure_dataset/val/labels, YOLO-format .txt files, one row per fish per image) and compute the fish-per-frame count distribution directly (histogram: how many frames have 0, 1, 2, ... fish). (2) Combine this distribution with the per-instance recall (0.719) under an independence-ish approximation to estimate P(a frame with k ground-truth fish has zero detections) -- e.g. for frames with low k (1-2 fish), a naive per-instance-independent model gives roughly (1-0.719)^k probability of a full miss, which must be stated as an approximation (detections are not truly independent per frame given shared lighting/occlusion) rather than an exact measurement; where possible, cross-check this estimate against actual model output on those specific low-k frames (run best.pt inference on them and directly count how many produce zero detections despite fish being present) rather than relying purely on the independence approximation. (3) Run an Ultralytics `model.val()` confidence-threshold sweep at 2-3 alternate operating points (e.g. conf=0.15, 0.25, 0.35 in addition to whatever the deployed default is) on best.pt against the same val set, recording precision/recall/F1 at each point, to confirm P=0.858/R=0.719 is the true F1-argmax or identify where the actual argmax lands. (4) State H7 with confident, unhedged language (per novelty_flags.json's OPEN/C7 status) in the Results/Discussion write-up, and carry MODEL_RAPORU.md's existing 'Kalan zayıf nokta: Recall ~0.72 -- yoğun/örtüşen balıklar kaçırılıyor' language forward as the carried Known Limitations #2 text, explicitly tracing the finding to backend/rules.py's `fish_count == 0` rule (confirmed: rules.py raises this to 'warning' severity specifically because a welfare monitor reporting zero fish is itself alarming).
experiments.required_environment: anaconda python3 (ultralytics) run from vision-service/ or repo root, mps device, no new model training. The fish-per-frame distribution step needs only label-file parsing (pure Python, no ML dependency). The confidence-threshold sweep needs Ultralytics val() re-runs, same cost class as EXP06's val() leg.
experiments.baselines: MODEL_RAPORU.md's current operating point: precision=0.858, recall=0.719 (epoch 77, corrected 2026-08-26), 98 val images / 1525 fish (~15.6 fish/frame average); backend/rules.py's fish_count==0 rule (confirmed at rules.py, raises status to 'warning') as the safety mechanism this finding is scoped against.
experiments.metrics: fish-per-frame histogram (count of frames per fish-count bucket); estimated and/or directly-measured full-frame-miss rate, ideally both an independence-approximation number and an empirically-measured number on the actual low-k frames; precision/recall/F1 at each swept confidence threshold; explicit statement of whether 0.858/0.719 is the argmax or where the true argmax lies.
experiments.ablations: The confidence-threshold sweep (2-3 alternate operating points vs. the deployed default) is the explicit ablation requested by G7's own success criteria.
experiments.success_criteria: Strong (matches G7 strong): fish-per-frame distribution computed directly from val labels; full-frame-miss rarity quantified numerically (not qualitatively); confidence-threshold sweep confirms or corrects the F1-argmax claim; H7 stated with confident language; Known Limitations #2 text carried forward, traced to rules.py's fish_count==0 rule. Minimum viable (matches G7 minimum_viable): if many val-set frames are sparse (1-2 fish), report the blind spot as MORE urgent than a narrow reading would suggest and state it as a specific numeric warning rather than a general caution -- itself a valid, reportable finding.
experiments.end_stage_rationale: The strong success criterion explicitly requires a confidence-threshold PR-curve sweep at multiple operating points to establish an F1-argmax claim, matching the task instructions' own example pattern for end_stage=4 (sweep-based strong criteria, as in G8).
open_decisions: The exact independence approximation for full-frame-miss probability from per-instance recall is a simplifying model, not something the codebase computes anywhere -- the researcher executing this must decide whether to report only the direct empirical count (run best.pt on actual low-k frames, count zero-detection outcomes) and treat the independence approximation as a secondary sanity-check, or lead with the approximation; the direct empirical count is recommended as the primary, more defensible number.

Which specific alternate confidence thresholds to sweep (this design proposes 0.15/0.25/0.35 as reasonable brackets around a typical Ultralytics default of 0.25, but the actual deployed threshold used in vision-service/yolo_runner.py was not independently re-confirmed in this design pass and should be read directly from that file before choosing sweep points).

experiments.title: MLOps PSI Drift-Binning Sweep (Quantile vs. Equal-Width) + Retrain Gate Exercise
addresses_questions: Does a systematic synthetic-degradation sweep confirm quantile-edge PSI binning grades smoothly where equal-width binning saturates, and does mlops/retrain.py's three-way decision path (none/review/retrain) plus its MIN_IMPROVEMENT gate behave as designed against synthetic no-drift and significant-drift windows?
experiments.hypothesis: H5: quantile-edge PSI binning (mlops/drift.py's current `bin_edges()`, which places interior cut points at the reference distribution's own deciles) produces a smooth, monotonically-informative PSI-vs-degradation-severity curve across many synthetic severities, whereas a reconstructed equal-width binning scheme (fixed [0,1] cut points) saturates/jumps discontinuously at some severities because the detector's confidence mass sits in a narrow ~0.5-0.9 band, leaving several fixed bins empty (per drift.py's own code-comment narrative of the historical 0.06->1.05 jump); separately, mlops/retrain.py's three-way decision logic (none/review/retrain, gated by MODERATE=0.10/SIGNIFICANT=0.25 thresholds) and its MIN_IMPROVEMENT=0.005 champion-challenger gate behave exactly as their code specifies when exercised against synthetic no-drift and significant-drift confidence windows.
experiments.procedure: (1) Load the existing reference confidence distribution from mlops/reference_confidence.json (confirmed present, 14,633 bytes -- already captured from the val set, no need to re-run `python -m mlops.drift --reference` unless it's stale/missing). (2) Write a synthetic-degradation generator that perturbs the reference distribution at many severities (e.g. a parametrized sweep: shift the mean by delta in {0.00, 0.02, 0.04, ..., 0.30} and/or inject an increasing fraction of low-confidence detections, covering a finer grid than the current '4 anecdotal points'). (3) For each severity, compute PSI twice: once using drift.py's existing quantile-edge `bin_edges()`/`histogram()`/`psi()` functions unmodified, and once using a newly-implemented equal-width binning variant (`[i/10 for i in range(1,10)]`, i.e. drift.py's own histogram() function already supports arbitrary edges via its `edges` parameter, so the equal-width variant is a one-line call: `histogram(values, edges=[i/10 for i in range(1,10)])` fed into a psi()-equivalent computation using those fixed edges for BOTH reference and current -- reuse psi()'s internal logic but pass equal-width edges instead of bin_edges(reference)). (4) Plot/tabulate the resulting quantile-vs-equal-width PSI curves across all swept severities to show where equal-width saturates/jumps and quantile grades smoothly (or report if they do not cleanly separate at every severity, per the minimum_viable clause). (5) Since `git log --oneline --all -- mlops/drift.py` returns exactly one commit (confirmed in this design pass), the historical 0.06->1.05 equal-width figures are NOT recoverable as measured history -- label the equal-width curve explicitly as a faithful reconstruction using the current codebase's own histogram()/psi() machinery with different edges, never as 'recovered from git.' (6) Construct two synthetic confidence windows (>=200 detections each, since MIN_WINDOW=200 per retrain.py) -- one a no-drift window (resampled from the reference itself) and one a significant-drift window (severity chosen from step 2's sweep to land above SIGNIFICANT=0.25) -- write each to a JSON file with a `confidences` key, and run `python -m mlops.retrain --check <file>.json` on both, recording the resulting action (none/review/retrain) and reason string. (7) Additionally construct a synthetic candidate mAP50 value and call `mlops.retrain.gate(candidate_map50, incumbent_map50)` directly (a pure function, no I/O) at three deltas: below 0, between 0 and MIN_IMPROVEMENT=0.005, and above MIN_IMPROVEMENT, to confirm the three-way gate behavior. (8) Cite source 23 (PSI/binning literature) and source 22 (champion-challenger MLOps) to frame H5 as known-best-practice application.
experiments.required_environment: Pure Python, no ML framework needed for the PSI sweep itself (mlops/drift.py's psi()/histogram()/bin_edges() have zero external dependencies beyond stdlib math/json) -- runs in the anaconda env or even the bare repo venv. mlops/retrain.py additionally imports mlops/tracking.py's mlflow wrapper only inside `incumbent_map50()`, which is wrapped in a try/except that returns None on failure, so `--check` runs fine even without a populated mlflow store for the 'none'/'review' actions; the 'retrain' action path additionally tries to read an incumbent mAP50 from the mlflow tracking store (mlops/mlflow.db, confirmed present) via mlops/tracking.py -- mlflow 3.15.1 confirmed importable in the anaconda env, so this should work, but has not been end-to-end tested in this design pass.
experiments.baselines: drift.py's own code-comment-narrated historical failure (PSI jumping 0.06->1.05 under equal-width binning) as the qualitative phenomenon this sweep must reproduce/reconstruct, explicitly labeled as reconstruction not measured history; retrain.py's MODERATE=0.10/SIGNIFICANT=0.25/MIN_IMPROVEMENT=0.005 constants as the exact decision-boundary values the exercise must land on either side of by construction.
experiments.metrics: PSI value per synthetic severity per binning scheme (two curves over the same severity grid); qualitative/quantitative characterization of where each curve saturates or jumps discontinuously vs. grades smoothly; retrain.py `decide()` action (none/review/retrain) for the two constructed windows; `gate()` boolean + reason string at three deltas relative to MIN_IMPROVEMENT.
experiments.ablations: The core deliverable IS the ablation: quantile-edge vs. equal-width binning, swept across many synthetic severities -- this is explicitly the sweep the task instructions cite as the canonical end_stage=4 example.
experiments.success_criteria: Strong (matches G8 strong): full many-severity sweep run through both binning schemes producing a smooth-vs-saturating comparison curve; retrain.py's three-way decision exercised on both a synthetic no-drift and significant-drift window with results reported; MIN_IMPROVEMENT gate exercised at 3 deltas; equal-width comparison explicitly labeled as reconstruction (confirmed necessary, since git history does not contain it); sources 22/23 cited. Minimum viable (matches G8 minimum_viable): if the sweep does not cleanly separate the two schemes at every severity, report exactly where it does and does not.
experiments.end_stage_rationale: This goal is the task instructions' own explicit example of end_stage=4 ('use end_stage=4 for goals whose strong success_criteria involves ablations or a sweep, e.g. G8') -- the binning-scheme comparison across many synthetic severities is exactly that sweep.
open_decisions: The exact synthetic-degradation severity grid (how many points, what perturbation model -- mean-shift vs. injected low-confidence fraction vs. both) is not specified anywhere upstream and must be designed by whoever executes this; a mean-shift sweep is the simplest and most directly comparable to drift.py's own mean_reference/mean_current reporting, but a more realistic degradation might combine mean-shift with increased variance.

Whether mlops/tracking.py's `incumbent_map50()` actually returns a usable value against the existing mlops/mlflow.db (needed for the full retrain.py 'retrain' action path's second-stage message, though not for the action decision itself) was not end-to-end tested in this design pass -- run `python -m mlops.retrain --check <significant_drift>.json` once early to confirm this path doesn't error before building the full sweep around it.

experiments.title: twin_bridge Mechanism-Evidence Inventory + New FakeTwin Edge-Case Test
addresses_questions: What does twin_bridge/test_bridge.py's existing unit-test suite, plus a new FakeTwin-scripted synthetic edge-case integration test, actually establish about compare_once()'s mechanism correctness -- and can this evidence be reported honestly as unit-tested-only without ever implying live cross-implementation corroboration that has not occurred?
experiments.hypothesis: sub_question_2_twin_bridge: twin_bridge/compare.py's `compare_once()` agree/expected/unexplained classification logic is correctly implemented per its own design (register scaling, alarm-bit decoding, the DO-low<->critical mapping, and the three named expected-divergence causes) as demonstrated by unit tests, and this mechanism-correctness evidence extends further once new edge cases -- specifically the combination of multiple simultaneous expected-divergence causes, and the structurally-reachable-but-currently-untested 'unmapped alarm string while do_low==sure_critical' branch inside compare_once -- are exercised via a FakeTwin-scripted integration test; none of this constitutes or should be described as live cross-implementation corroboration against an actual running PLC/Godot session.
experiments.procedure: (1) Run `python -m pytest twin_bridge/test_bridge.py -v` (confirmed runnable: pure pytest, no external services, `sys.path` self-contained) and record the full pass/fail list of its existing ~18 test functions as mechanism-correctness evidence. (2) Write a new test file (or extend test_bridge.py) adding a FakeTwin-scripted synthetic edge-case integration test exercising `compare_once()` end-to-end for cases NOT currently covered, specifically: (a) multiple simultaneous expected-divergence causes firing together (e.g. `_input(alarms=0b1110)` -- ammonia + temperature + stress all raised at once with DO fine and S.U.R.E. status 'ok', asserting `kind=='expected'` and that the note lists all three reasons via EXPECTED_DIVERGENCE); (b) the currently-unreachable-via-decode_alarms 'unmapped alarm string' branch inside compare_once (lines ~90-98 of twin_bridge/compare.py) by directly constructing an `inputs` dict with `alarms=['dissolved oxygen low', 'some_new_sensor_fault']` (bypassing decode_alarms entirely, which a FakeTwin-based test CAN do since compare_once takes raw dicts) with matching DO status, asserting `kind=='unexplained'` and the note names the unmapped alarm -- this directly tests a genuine gap identified in this design pass, not a re-statement of existing coverage; (c) a full multi-sample `run()` session via FakeTwin scripting a mix of agree/expected/unexplained frames in sequence (extending the existing `test_run_tallies_agreement_over_a_session` pattern) to confirm the `Comparison` aggregate counters (agree/expected/unexplained) correctly separate all three kinds within one session, not just two-at-a-time as the existing test does. (3) Write the Results 5.6 / Known Limitations #4 paragraph stating twin_bridge's status exactly as 'designed and unit-tested (test_bridge.py), not exercised against a live twin session,' with 'validated' never used absent an actual live run -- and explicitly note the FakeTwin-scripted tests are team-scripted mechanism evidence, never cross-implementation corroboration (frames are authored by the same team that wrote compare.py, not independently produced by Godot/CODESYS).
experiments.required_environment: Any Python with pytest installed (confirmed: pytest 8.4.2 in the anaconda env; pydantic not needed here since twin_bridge has zero pydantic/fastapi/httpx dependencies by design, per client.py's own docstring). No PLC, no Godot, no network -- runs in well under a second.
experiments.baselines: The existing test_bridge.py's own coverage (confirmed: agree x2, one expected-divergence case, unexplained x2) as the floor this experiment must not merely repeat but extend; TB-3 (a live Godot/CODESYS session) as the explicitly-excluded higher-risk alternative this goal deliberately does not attempt.
experiments.metrics: pytest pass/fail count for the existing suite (expect all green, confirming no regression); pass/fail for the >=3 new edge-case tests; a coverage inventory table (which agree/expected/unexplained sub-cases are and are not exercised, before and after this experiment's additions).
experiments.ablations: Not applicable -- this is a test-coverage/mechanism-evidence goal, not a parametrized measurement.
experiments.success_criteria: Strong (matches G9 strong, which the goal's own success_criteria note IS its minimum-viable form): existing test_bridge.py suite passes; new FakeTwin-scripted edge-case test(s) added and passing, covering at least the register-mismatch/within-tolerance/unexplained-divergence categories named in research_goals.json; Results 5.6 paragraph written with the exact honest-status language and 'validated' never used absent a live session. No separate minimum_viable exists beyond this -- per research_goals.json, this goal's success criteria are already its own floor, requiring no infrastructure beyond what is already in the repo.
experiments.end_stage_rationale: No sweep or ablation applies to a unit/integration-test-coverage goal; this is the paper's designated fallback goal with a single achievable success bar (its own success_criteria field states the strong and minimum_viable criteria are identical), so end_stage=3 (full run for that one bar) is correct and end_stage=4 would be spurious.
open_decisions: Whether TB-3's live Godot/CODESYS go/no-go checkpoint (mentioned in research_plan.md as occurring one week before manuscript freeze) has already passed or is still pending was not checked in this design pass -- if it has already resolved to 'no-go' (confirmed likely per research_plan.md's own 'High likelihood' risk assessment and the fact that no Godot/CODESYS installation or capture-adapter script was found anywhere in this codebase during verification), this experiment's scope is exactly as described above with no live-session upgrade; if a live session materializes, that is an upgrade to report separately, per G9's own fallback_rationale, not a replacement for this experiment.

The exact register/alarm-bit values for the two new synthetic edge cases in step 2 above (e.g. which specific alarms combination) are proposed concretely in the procedure but the researcher executing this may choose to add further edge cases (e.g. a within-tolerance-but-not-exact DO boundary case near the rules.py 6.0 mg/L threshold) -- this is a reasonable extension, not a required one.

experiments.title: Cross-Layer Thesis Framing Decision + Confirmatory Literature Search
addresses_questions: Does one additional targeted literature search confirm (or force a narrowing of) the central cross-layer thesis (C2) as the paper's headline framing, and which of the three framing options (foreground/separate/hybrid) best matches the evidence actually produced by G3, G4, G6, G7, G8, and G9?
experiments.hypothesis: central_cross_layer_thesis_C2: no prior published work demonstrates deterministic, escalation-only authority applied and empirically measured across five architecturally distinct probabilistic layers (LLM severity reasoning, agentic tool routing, RAG retrieval, MLOps retrain-gating, edge vision) within one deployed system -- confirmable at medium-to-high confidence via one additional targeted search beyond literature_review_matrix.md's existing Theme 3 sources (11, 26, 12, 13, 14.1) -- and CT-3 (the hybrid framing: eval-harness-drift incident as narrative hook, cross-layer thesis stated with an explicit medium-confidence caveat) is the framing best supported once G3/G4/G6/G7/G8/G9's actual (not assumed) results are in hand.
experiments.procedure: This is a literature-search-and-synthesis goal, not a codebase measurement -- it depends on EXP03/EXP04/EXP06/EXP07/EXP08/EXP09's actual outputs (dependencies: G3, G4, G6, G7, G8, G9 per research_goals.json) and cannot be meaningfully executed until those land. (1) Run one additional targeted literature search (CT-4's own suggested query, e.g. 'multi-layer AI governance case study deployed system' or an equivalent formulation, plus 1-2 variant phrasings such as 'deterministic safety layer probabilistic AI industrial deployment' and 'cross-component guardrail architecture empirical evaluation') using whatever web/literature search tool is available at execution time (not available inside this codebase-analysis pass) to check for a closer prior instance of the cross-layer claim than literature_review_matrix.md's existing Theme 3 entries. (2) Read back through EXP03/EXP04/EXP06/EXP07/EXP08/EXP09's actual completed results (not this design document's predictions of what they might find) to determine which framing option (CT-1 foreground / CT-2 separate / CT-3 hybrid) the real evidence supports -- e.g. if EXP04 (G4) or EXP06 (G6) surfaced a materially softened or downgraded finding, that pulls toward CT-2's more conservative framing; if all layers held up cleanly, CT-3 (or even CT-1) is better supported. (3) Write the one-paragraph framing decision and justification, plus a draft Abstract/Conclusion sentence instantiating the chosen framing, explicitly hedged to C2's OPEN-but-medium-confidence novelty status per novelty_flags.json.
experiments.required_environment: A literature/web search capability (not part of the codebase-analysis toolset used to produce this design) plus access to EXP01-EXP09's completed outputs. No code execution against the sure-project repo is required for this goal itself.
experiments.baselines: literature_review_matrix.md's existing Theme 3 sources (11, 26, 12, 13, 14.1: SIS/IEC 61511, RL shielding, guardrail industry blogs, LLM-industrial-control academic work) as the prior-art floor this search must confirm remains the closest existing work, or else identify what is closer.
experiments.metrics: Not a numeric experiment -- the 'metric' is a confidence classification (medium-to-high vs. narrowed) for C2's novelty claim, and a categorical framing choice (CT-1/CT-2/CT-3) with written justification.
experiments.ablations: The three mutually-exclusive framing options (CT-1/CT-2/CT-3) function as the decision space this goal chooses among, not a swept parameter with a numeric outcome.
experiments.success_criteria: Strong (matches G10 strong): search confirms medium-to-high confidence no closer prior instance exists; CT-3 selected and justified as the paper's framing, synthesizing the completed G3/G4/G6/G7/G8/G9 results. Minimum viable (matches G10 minimum_viable): if the search surfaces a closer prior instance, narrow C2's claim accordingly (report the found source and the specific narrowing) rather than retracting the cross-layer observation entirely -- CT-2's more conservative framing remains valid and reportable even if CT-1/CT-3 must be softened.
experiments.end_stage_rationale: A literature-confirmation-plus-framing-decision goal has no ablation/sweep structure of its own; end_stage=3 applies once the underlying layer-level experiments (EXP03/04/06/07/08/09) it synthesizes have completed.
open_decisions: This experiment cannot actually be executed until EXP03, EXP04, EXP06, EXP07, EXP08, and EXP09 have all produced real results -- it is sequenced last among the primary experiments by hard dependency, not by choice, and any attempt to pre-write its conclusion before those land would be exactly the kind of unfounded claim this whole design pass is trying to avoid.

No web-search tool was exercised as part of this design pass (the design task was scoped to codebase verification only) -- the actual CT-4 query wording and result interpretation is left entirely to the execution phase.

experiments.title: Manuscript-Wide Stale-Figure Grep + Commit-Hash Provenance Table
addresses_questions: Does a manuscript-wide grep pass confirm the stale 0.695 recall figure never ships, and is every re-measured number across G1-G9 traceable to an exact git commit hash and date?
experiments.hypothesis: cross-cutting: the stale pre-correction recall figure of 0.695 (confirmed still present in TODOS.md line 11: 'sure_v1 recall ~0.695' -- a known, already-acknowledged-stale planning document, not the manuscript) never appears anywhere in the actual paper draft or paper_workspace artifacts in place of the corrected 0.719 (MODEL_RAPORU.md's 2026-08-26 correction), and every re-measured number produced by EXP01-EXP09 can be attached to the exact git commit hash and date it was measured against.
experiments.procedure: (1) Once a manuscript draft exists (this goal depends on G1-G9 per research_goals.json, i.e. on EXP01-EXP09's completion), run `grep -rn '0.695' <manuscript files> <paper_workspace artifacts>` and confirm zero hits in anything that ships (a hit in TODOS.md itself, which is explicitly a pre-existing, already-acknowledged-stale initial_context document rather than manuscript output, is expected and not a failure -- confirmed present at repo root TODOS.md line 11 in this design pass, and its own text already flags it as the pre-correction number ('P2' priority item written before the epoch-77 correction landed)). Additionally grep for the corrected figure's absence-of-substitution risk by checking every occurrence of 'recall' near a vision-context number resolves to 0.719, not any other stale value. (2) Build a provenance table: for each re-measured number produced by EXP01 (RAG sweep argmax/MRR/hit@1), EXP02 (consistency-check pass/fail), EXP03 (eval.py+apply_rule_override bucket counts, test_decision.py pass/fail), EXP04 (bench_agent.py format/selection %s, old and new scenario counts), EXP05 (leakage-audit collision count), EXP06 (export_bench.py six-config table, multi-session CoreML variance, ONNX/TorchScript IoU-overlap), EXP07 (fish-per-frame distribution, full-frame-miss rate, PR-sweep argmax), EXP08 (PSI sweep curves, retrain.py decisions), EXP09 (pytest pass counts) -- record the exact `git rev-parse HEAD` short hash and ISO date at the moment each was measured, consolidated into one appendix table.
experiments.required_environment: Plain shell grep + access to the manuscript draft and all of EXP01-EXP09's output artifacts once produced. No code execution against the sure-project repo beyond `git rev-parse HEAD` / `git log -1 --format=%cd` at each experiment's run time (which should be captured AS PART of running EXP01-EXP09, not reconstructed after the fact).
experiments.baselines: TODOS.md's already-known-stale 0.695 figure (confirmed present, line 11, in a pre-correction planning document) as the specific string this grep must guarantee never leaks into the manuscript; MODEL_RAPORU.md's corrected 0.719 as the value every manuscript occurrence of vision recall must resolve to; git HEAD at design time (3c1b9fabf7a5de59e83b81965d1a319498baaec5, 2026-08-26) as the provenance anchor for numbers measured today, noting later experiments may run against later commits if the repo changes before manuscript freeze.
experiments.metrics: count of '0.695' occurrences in shippable manuscript text (target: 0); count of vision-recall mentions correctly resolving to 0.719 (target: 100%); count of EXP01-EXP09 numbers with an attached commit-hash+date (target: 100%, or per minimum_viable, at least EXP01/EXP03/EXP06's highest-priority numbers).
experiments.ablations: Not applicable -- this is a manuscript QA pass, not a measurement with tunable parameters.
experiments.success_criteria: Strong (matches G11 strong): grep pass confirms zero stale-0.695 occurrences in shippable text and 100% resolution to 0.719; every EXP01-EXP09 re-measured number has an attached commit hash/date in one consolidated provenance table/appendix. Minimum viable (matches G11 minimum_viable): if full commit-hash provenance cannot be attached to every number before freeze, at minimum guarantee the 0.695-vs-0.719 grep check passes and record provenance for EXP01's RAG sweep, EXP03's eval.py run, and EXP06's export_bench.py table specifically (the three numbers research_goals.json itself names as highest-priority).
experiments.end_stage_rationale: A grep-and-provenance QA pass has no ablation/sweep dimension; end_stage=3 for the full run once its dependencies (all of EXP01-EXP09) exist. It is sequenced last of all 11 experiments, matching research_goals.json's own priority=12 (highest number, i.e. last).
open_decisions: No manuscript draft exists yet at the time of this design pass (only paper_workspace planning artifacts) -- this experiment is not executable until a draft exists, which itself depends on EXP01-EXP09's completion and G10's framing decision (EXP10) feeding into the actual prose; this design spec describes the QA procedure to run once that draft exists, not something runnable today.

Whether every one of EXP01-EXP09 will in practice log its own git commit hash/date at run time (recommended) or whether this experiment must reconstruct it after the fact from file mtimes/git blame on wherever results were saved is an operational choice for the execution phase -- logging it live during each experiment is strongly preferable and should be written into each of EXP01-EXP09's own output format now, before they run.
